name: ellm-provider
description: Use a chat-only, token-authenticated enterprise LLM as a model in VS Code chat and agent mode

ellm.url.markdownDescription: Base URL of the enterprise LLM, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:9800`. Set this from **Enterprise LLM: Configure Connection**.

ellm.authHeader.markdownDescription: HTTP header the auth token is sent in. Many APIs want `Authorization` instead — set `#ellm.authPrefix#` to `Bearer ` if so.

ellm.authPrefix.markdownDescription: Text placed before the token in the auth header, e.g. `Bearer ` (keep the trailing space). Empty means the raw token is sent.

ellm.maxResponseChars.description: Hard per-response character cap the upstream enforces. Responses that hit it are automatically continued and stitched. 0 disables continuation.

ellm.contextChars.markdownDescription: How many characters of prompt the backend accepts in one request. This is what the model advertises to VS Code as its context window, and VS Code fills it — so if it is set higher than the backend allows, the backend truncates, and it truncates the START of the prompt, where the tool definitions are. There is no discovery endpoint, so this cannot be detected: lower it if long conversations start ignoring tools.

ellm.maxContinuations.description: Safety limit on how many times one answer may be continued. A file written through the response cap needs one round per cap-full of text, so a large file needs many.

enumDescriptions: VS Code global storage — this machine, all folders. Not encrypted.
VS Code workspace storage — this folder only. Not encrypted.
OS keychain via SecretStorage. Encrypted, but unavailable on some managed machines.
ellm.tokenStorage.markdownDescription: Where the auth token is stored. `keychain` is the only encrypted option, but locked-down machines may refuse it — in that case the token falls back to global storage and the panel tells you.

ellm.chatPath.markdownDescription: Path of the streaming chat endpoint, appended to `#ellm.url#`. Set it from **Enterprise LLM: Configure Connection**.

ellm.models.markdownDescription: Comma-separated model names, exactly as the backend names them. There is no discovery endpoint, so this is the model list shown in the picker.

ellm.textPath.markdownDescription: Dot-path to the text inside a streamed frame, e.g. `delta.text`. Leave blank to auto-detect; set it if the auto-detect picks the wrong field.

ellm.servedModelPath.markdownDescription: Dot-path to the model name inside a streamed frame, e.g. `metadata.model`. Leave blank to auto-detect. Used to warn when the backend serves a different model than the one you picked — an unknown model name is usually answered with the backend's default rather than an error.

ellm.promptField.markdownDescription: Body field the prompt is sent in, e.g. `prompt`, `message`, `input`. Whatever your backend calls it.

enumDescriptions: Log only the model field and value.
Log the body's key names and value types — enough to find the field that selects the model.
Log the whole body. Credentials and the prompt are still hidden.
ellm.logRequestBody.markdownDescription: How much of each outgoing request to write to the **Enterprise LLM** output channel — the equivalent of reading the payload in your browser's DevTools. `keys` shows the shape only; `full` shows the values. Credential-looking fields and the prompt itself are hidden in both. Use it to compare what the extension sends against what the web app sends, then turn it back `off`.

ellm.modelField.markdownDescription: Body field the picked model is sent in, e.g. `model`, `modelId`, `engine`. Whatever your backend calls it. **If this is not the key your backend actually reads, the model picker has no effect** — the name goes into a field the backend ignores and it answers from its default instead, which looks identical to a working setup.
